# Conversion

mulle-utf converts between UTF-8, UTF-16 and UTF-32 in host byte order.
All UTF-16 and UTF-32 data is assumed to be in the native byte order of the
platform. There is no BOM-based byte-swapping or explicit LE/BE variant.

The preferred and safe way to do the conversion is using the buffer routines
in conjunction with [mulle-buffer](//github.com/mulle-nat/mulle-buffer).

Here is an example how to convert a UTF-8 string into UTF-32 using a
`mulle_buffer`:

``` c
   struct mulle_buffer   buffer;
   mulle_utf32_t         *s;

   mulle_buffer_init( &buffer, NULL);
   mulle_utf8_bufferconvert_to_utf32( "VfL Bochum 1848",
                                      (size_t) -1,
                                      &buffer,
                                      mulle_buffer_add_bytes);
   s = mulle_buffer_extract( &buffer);
   mulle_buffer_done( &buffer);
   mulle_free( s);
```


## Buffer functions

These are the low-level conversion functions. The input is assumed to be
well-formed and valid. For UTF data of unknown source, you should run
`mulle_utf8_information` (or the UTF-16/UTF-32 equivalent) before conversion
to validate the input and determine output lengths.

These functions return `void`. They do not validate; passing malformed input
is undefined behaviour.

### `mulle_utf8_bufferconvert_to_utf16`

``` c
void   mulle_utf8_bufferconvert_to_utf16( char *src,
                                          size_t len,
                                          void *buffer,
                                          mulle_utf_add_bytes_function_t *addbytes);
```

Convert up to `len` bytes of UTF-8 string `src` to UTF-16 in host byte order.
You may pass `(size_t) -1` for `len` to let the function determine the length
of `src` with `strlen`. It is OK to have `\0` in your `src` data when an
explicit length is given.

The `addbytes` function is called repeatedly with chunks of converted
`mulle_utf16_t` characters. There will be no trailing zero character.

Example: A conversion of a single character string "A" would result in a
call to `addbytes` like this:

``` c
mulle_utf16_t   c;

c = 'A';
(*addbytes)( buffer, &c, sizeof( mulle_utf16_t));
```


### All buffer conversion functions

``` c
void  mulle_utf8_bufferconvert_to_utf16( char *src, size_t len,
                                         void *buffer,
                                         mulle_utf_add_bytes_function_t *addbytes);
void  mulle_utf8_bufferconvert_to_utf32( char *src, size_t len,
                                         void *buffer,
                                         mulle_utf_add_bytes_function_t *addbytes);
void  mulle_utf16_bufferconvert_to_utf8( mulle_utf16_t *src, size_t len,
                                         void *buffer,
                                         mulle_utf_add_bytes_function_t *addbytes);
void  mulle_utf16_bufferconvert_to_utf32( mulle_utf16_t *src, size_t len,
                                          void *buffer,
                                          mulle_utf_add_bytes_function_t *addbytes);
void  mulle_utf32_bufferconvert_to_utf8( mulle_utf32_t *src, size_t len,
                                         void *buffer,
                                         mulle_utf_add_bytes_function_t *addbytes);
void  mulle_utf32_bufferconvert_to_utf16( mulle_utf32_t *src, size_t len,
                                          void *buffer,
                                          mulle_utf_add_bytes_function_t *addbytes);
```


## Allocator functions

These functions validate the input, allocate output using the provided
allocator, convert, and return a zero-terminated result. They are built on
the buffer routines internally.

### `mulle_utf8_convert_to_utf16_string`

``` c
mulle_utf16_t  *mulle_utf8_convert_to_utf16_string( char *src,
                                                    size_t len,
                                                    struct mulle_allocator *allocator);
```

Convert up to `len` bytes of UTF-8 string `src` to a zero-terminated UTF-16
string allocated with `allocator`. Returns `NULL` with `errno` set to `EINVAL`
if `src` is not valid UTF-8. If `src` contains `\0`, conversion will stop there.

### All allocator conversion functions

``` c
mulle_utf16_t  *mulle_utf8_convert_to_utf16_string( char *src, size_t len,
                                                    struct mulle_allocator *allocator);
mulle_utf32_t  *mulle_utf8_convert_to_utf32_string( char *src, size_t len,
                                                    struct mulle_allocator *allocator);
char           *mulle_utf16_convert_to_utf8_string( mulle_utf16_t *src, size_t len,
                                                    struct mulle_allocator *allocator);
mulle_utf32_t  *mulle_utf16_convert_to_utf32_string( mulle_utf16_t *src, size_t len,
                                                     struct mulle_allocator *allocator);
char           *mulle_utf32_convert_to_utf8_string( mulle_utf32_t *src, size_t len,
                                                    struct mulle_allocator *allocator);
mulle_utf16_t  *mulle_utf32_convert_to_utf16_string( mulle_utf32_t *src, size_t len,
                                                     struct mulle_allocator *allocator);
```

All return `NULL` with `errno = EINVAL` on invalid input.


## Low-level (unchecked) functions

These write into a caller-supplied buffer with no validation or bounds
checking. The caller must ensure the input is valid and the output buffer is
large enough (use the `information` or length functions to determine sizes).

``` c
char          *_mulle_utf32_convert_to_utf8( mulle_utf32_t *src, size_t len, char *dst);
mulle_utf16_t *_mulle_utf32_convert_to_utf16( mulle_utf32_t *src, size_t len, mulle_utf16_t *dst);
char          *_mulle_utf16_convert_to_utf8( mulle_utf16_t *src, size_t len, char *dst);
mulle_utf32_t *_mulle_utf16_convert_to_utf32( mulle_utf16_t *src, size_t len, mulle_utf32_t *dst);
mulle_utf16_t *_mulle_utf8_convert_to_utf16( char *src, size_t len, mulle_utf16_t *dst);
mulle_utf32_t *_mulle_utf8_convert_to_utf32( char *src, size_t len, mulle_utf32_t *dst);
```

All return a pointer past the last element written.
